subject: Archaeology
title: The First Villages: Jericho
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The First Villages: Jericho.

hook.text: Jericho may be the oldest continuously inhabited city on Earth. People have lived there for over 11,000 years.

buildup.text: The earliest settlement had round mud-brick houses and a massive stone tower dating to 8000 BCE — the oldest known.

discovery.text: The tower is 28 feet tall and required organized labor. A small farming village built a monument before pyramids.

twist.text: Residents plastered and painted skulls of their dead and displayed them in houses — an ancestor worship practice.

climax.text: Jericho shows that permanent settlement, monumental building, and complex ritual all appeared before pottery was.

punchline.text: They built a tower 10,000 years ago. They had not yet invented a clay pot.

quiz.question: What makes Jericho's stone tower remarkable?
options: It is the tallest ancient structure in the Middle East
It is the oldest known tower, built before pottery was invented
It was used as an astronomical observatory
